problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(-3,0),(3,0),$ and $(0,-3).$ Which of the following are coordinates of a vertex of ${S}^{′}$, the image of $S$ under the action of $T?$

- $(21,0)$
- $(3,0)$
- $(-21,0)$
worked_solution:
To find the image of $S$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-21 & 21 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(-21,0),(21,0),(0,3).$ 

So, the correct answer is "I and III only."
